We have the ability to cheaply provide the equivalent of very good personalized human help in any language to anyone with a cellphone. This suggests some wicked problems in education, healthcare, development, etc. might now be tractable. I don't see enough ambition to solve them

I have worked on issues like financial literacy and democratizing education for years, and so much work went into trying to figure out ways to substitute for the fact that what we really needed was a well-trained human being to work with each learner. Human help never scaled.

Tom Mueller, SpaceX employee #1, says Elon Musk reversed his approach to engineering by demanding they find where rocket engines break and then push them harder "It changed just working with Elon. At my previous company, it was like, you never blow up a rocket engine or fail a rocket engine. That's bad. This is bad karma. Never test, always have a lot of margin and make sure that you don't fail it." "And Elon's whole thing was, well, let's find out where it breaks and then fix that and go and push it even more. So it's really a whole different way of thinking about it. Really refreshing, and you learn a lot." "We had things that we thought would break that we couldn't break. Other things would break because the engineering is not always that deterministic. It's not always obvious. I'm amazed that this thing is still running."
